prompt: $5$ scores have mean $80$. If a $6$th score of $74$ is added, the new mean is approximately:
hint: You do not know the five scores, but the mean tells you what they add up to.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Use a sample of 3–4 values to see how the rule works, then apply it to the real data.
You do not know the five scores, but the mean tells you what they add up to.
The five scores total $5 \times 80 = 400$. Adding the score of $74$ gives $474$, and now there are $6$ scores to share that total.

explanation: The mean times the count gives the total, so the first five scores add to $5 \times 80 = 400$.
Add the sixth score to that total: $400 + 74 = 474$.
There are now $6$ scores, so the new total is divided by $6$.
Dividing gives $474 \div 6 = 79$, so the new mean is $79$.
